task1.title: Car ownership in Britain, 1975–2005
task1.prompt: The graph below gives information about car ownership in Britain from 1975 to 2005.

chartDesc.overview: Having 1 car remained the most common status throughout the 30-year period, while the proportion of households with no car fell dramatically. Conversely, ownership of 2 cars and 3 cars both showed a steady increase over time.
unreadable: Exact values for points not landing precisely on gridlines must be visually estimated as numerical labels are not printed on the markers.
keyFeatures: 1 car was consistently the highest proportion, standing at 45% in 1975 and finishing at approximately 44.5% in 2005.
No car experienced the largest decline, dropping significantly from around 42% in 1975 to 25% in 1985, and further to about 21.5% in 2005.
2 cars increased significantly from about 6.5% in 1975 to 18% in 2005.
3 cars remained the lowest percentage throughout, but tripled from 3% in 1975 to 9% in 2005.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The line graph shows what percentage of British households owned no car, one car, two cars or three cars at ten-year intervals between 1975 and 2005.

Overall, car ownership rose markedly over the period: the proportion of households with two or three cars grew, while the share with no car fell sharply. Single-car ownership remained the most common situation throughout, whereas three-car households were consistently the rarest.

The most dramatic change concerned households without a car. In 1975 these made up 42% of the total, second only to one-car homes, but the figure plummeted to 25% by 1985 and then declined more gently to about 21% in 2005. Meanwhile, ownership of two cars followed the opposite path, climbing steadily from just 6% in 1975 to 14% in 1985 and reaching 18% by the end of the period.

One-car households remained dominant across all four decades, dipping from 45% in 1975 to 37% in 1985 before recovering to around 45% in 2005. Three-car ownership, though always the smallest category, crept up steadily from just 3% to 9%, effectively tripling. Taken together, these trends show a clear shift towards multi-car ownership as fewer and fewer British households did without a vehicle.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Chiziqli grafik 1975–2005-yillarda o'n yillik oraliqlarda Britaniya xonadonlarining necha foizi avtomobilsiz, bitta, ikkita yoki uchta avtomobilga ega bo'lganini ko'rsatadi.

Umuman olganda, davr mobaynida avtomobil egaligi sezilarli oshgan: ikki yoki uchta avtomobilli xonadonlar ulushi o'sgan, avtomobilsizlar ulushi esa keskin pasaygan. Bitta avtomobilga egalik boshdan-oxir eng keng tarqalgan holat bo'lib qolgan, uchta avtomobilli xonadonlar esa doimiy ravishda eng kam uchraydigani bo'lgan.

Eng keskin o'zgarish avtomobilsiz xonadonlarga tegishli. 1975-yilda ular jamining 42 foizini tashkil etib, bir avtomobilli uylardan keyin ikkinchi o'rinda turgan, biroq bu ko'rsatkich 1985-yilga kelib 25 foizga keskin tushib ketdi, so'ng 2005-yilda taxminan 21 foizga ancha ohista pasaydi. Ayni paytda ikki avtomobil egaligi qarama-qarshi yo'ldan bordi: 1975-yildagi atigi 6 foizdan 1985-yilda 14 foizga barqaror ko'tarilib, davr oxiriga kelib 18 foizga yetdi.

Bir avtomobilli xonadonlar to'rt o'n yillik davomida yetakchi bo'lib qoldi: 1975-yildagi 45 foizdan 1985-yilda 37 foizga tushib, so'ng 2005-yilda taxminan 45 foizga tiklandi. Uchta avtomobil egaligi doim eng kichik toifa bo'lsa-da, atigi 3 foizdan 9 foizga barqaror sekin ko'tarilib, aslida uch baravar oshdi. Birgalikda olganda, bu tendensiyalar tobora kamroq Britaniya xonadoni avtomobilsiz qolgani sari ko'p avtomobilga egalik tomon yaqqol siljishni ko'rsatadi.

task2.title: Why studying at university feels harder than school
task2.prompt: Many students find it harder to study at university or college than they did at school. Why is this? What can be done to solve this problem?
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
Many young people report that studying at university or college feels considerably harder than school ever did. In my view this difficulty stems mainly from the sudden demand for independent learning, and it can be eased through better preparation and support.

Several factors explain why higher education feels so tough. The most important is the shift in learning style. At school, teachers set daily tasks, monitor progress closely and remind pupils of every deadline, whereas university students must manage their own time, motivate themselves and study largely alone. The academic content is also far more demanding: instead of memorising facts, students are expected to think critically, read widely and produce original analysis. On top of this, many leave home for the first time and must juggle cooking, budgeting and often part-time work, so homesickness and financial stress add to the pressure. For students studying in a second language, the challenge is greater still.

Fortunately, this problem can be addressed at several levels. Schools could do more to build the self-study skills and time management that universities demand, for instance by gradually giving older pupils more independent projects. Universities, for their part, can ease the transition through induction courses, smaller first-year tutorials, accessible counselling services and clear guidance on academic writing. Students themselves also benefit from forming study groups and seeking help early rather than struggling in silence.

In conclusion, university feels harder than school mainly because it demands independence and deeper thinking at a time of great personal change. With better preparation in schools and stronger support at university, however, this difficulty can be significantly reduced.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Ko'plab yoshlar universitet yoki kollejda o'qish maktabdagidan ancha qiyinroq tuyulishini aytadi. Menimcha, bu qiyinchilik asosan mustaqil o'qishga bo'lgan to'satdan talabdan kelib chiqadi va uni yaxshiroq tayyorgarlik hamda yordam orqali yengillashtirish mumkin.

Oliy ta'lim nega shunchalik og'ir tuyulishini bir qancha omil izohlaydi. Eng muhimi — o'qish uslubidagi o'zgarish. Maktabda o'qituvchilar kundalik vazifalar beradi, o'zlashtirishni yaqindan kuzatadi va o'quvchilarga har bir muddatni eslatadi, universitet talabalari esa o'z vaqtini o'zi boshqarishi, o'zini rag'batlantirishi va asosan yolg'iz o'qishi kerak. Akademik mazmun ham ancha talabchan: faktlarni yodlash o'rniga talabalardan tanqidiy fikrlash, keng mutolaa qilish va original tahlil ishlab chiqarish kutiladi. Bundan tashqari, ko'pchilik birinchi marta uydan chiqadi va ovqat pishirish, byudjetni boshqarish, ko'pincha yarim kunlik ish bilan shug'ullanishga majbur bo'ladi, shu bois uyni sog'inish va moliyaviy stress bosimni yanada oshiradi. Ikkinchi tilda o'qiyotgan talabalar uchun bu sinov yanada kattaroq.

Baxtga qarshi emas, bu muammoni bir necha darajada hal qilish mumkin. Maktablar universitetlar talab qiladigan mustaqil o'qish ko'nikmalari va vaqtni boshqarishni ko'proq shakllantirishi mumkin — masalan, katta yoshdagi o'quvchilarga asta-sekin ko'proq mustaqil loyihalar berish orqali. Universitetlar esa o'tish davrini tanishtiruv kurslari, birinchi kurs uchun kichikroq mashg'ulotlar, qulay psixologik yordam xizmatlari va akademik yozuv bo'yicha aniq yo'l-yo'riq orqali yengillashtira oladi. Talabalarning o'zlari ham o'quv guruhlari tuzib, jimgina qiynalish o'rniga erta yordam so'rashdan naf ko'radi.

Xulosa qilib aytganda, universitet maktabdan ko'ra qiyinroq tuyuladi, chunki u katta shaxsiy o'zgarishlar davrida mustaqillik va chuqurroq fikrlashni talab qiladi. Biroq maktablarda yaxshiroq tayyorgarlik va universitetda kuchliroq yordam bilan bu qiyinchilikni sezilarli kamaytirish mumkin.
